title: GENERAL SOLVENTS/CLEANERS - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES
question: What is the recommended procedure for ensuring that a surface is thoroughly cleaned of oil, grease, or dirt before bonding or priming using solvents?
answer:
NOTE: This procedure applies specifically to aircraft models with engine nacelle configurations post-2015. For older models, refer to AMM revision 22B or later. Always verify tool availability before beginning.

Solvents exhibit a selective solvent action which permits its use in the removal of oil, grease or dirt. For selection of proper solvent, refer to Table 201. For the cleaning of metal, plastics or rubber, proceed Prior to bonding or priming, lightly abrade surface with either a ScotchBrite pad or (a) Wipe off all excess oil, grease or dirt from surface. (b) Apply solvent to a clean cloth by pouring solvent on the cloth from a safety can or other approved container. The cloth should be well saturated but not to the point of dripping. Wipe the surface with the moistened cloth as required to dissolve or loosen soil. Work on small enough area so the surface being cleaned remains wet. (d) With a clean dry cloth, immediately wipe the surface while the solvent is still wet. Do not allow the surface to evaporate dry. (e) Repeat steps (b) through (d) until there is no discoloration on the drying cloth. be used in place of Type I Use as a solvent or thinner

question: What are the recommended safety practices for recognizing and responding to symptoms of poisoning from toxic solvents during aircraft maintenance?
answer: Solvents are composed of a group of chemicals that often proves toxic.
